content: The term gender-blind or unisex refers to activities and services that are conducted or provided without considering the gender of the participants involved. The term unisex is considered outdated and somewhat misleading, as it literally means one sex. Some individuals believe it implies a dual-sex concept, which would mean two sexes at the same time. Many people avoid using the more accurate term bisex due to its sexual connotations. In contrast, the term gender-blind challenges the principles of heteronormativity by disregarding gender entirely. In 2006, the National Student Genderblind Campaign (NSGC) was established as a grassroots organization aimed at educating college students, administrators, and others across the country. The NSGC advocates for the adoption of gender-inclusive dormitory and bathroom options. The primary objective of the gender-blind dormitory policy campaign is to allow roommates to be assigned without regard to anyone's sex. Proponents of this proposal argue that it would enable transgender individuals and those who reject traditional gender labels to live in more comfortable environments than what is typically available in single-sex housing. They also assert that this policy would benefit heterosexual individuals who otherwise would not be able to live with their partners while attending university. In December 2006, the National Student Genderblind Campaign became embroiled in a national controversy after claiming to have received biased and negligent coverage from Boston's Fox 25 News. This controversy led to the release of a formal press statement on a national level and an appearance on Fox News Channel's Heartland show with John Kasich on December 16, 2006.
